name: sear-notch
title: Sear Notch
description: An alert-rule builder where the rule is a notch cut directly into a live historical sparkline: drag the floor to set the threshold, drag the shoulder apart to set the required dwell duration, and every past excursion is replayed against that exact rule so hollow near-misses flip solid as you tune it.
useWhen: authoring or tuning an alert rule against real history — a threshold AND a required dwell duration, where the backtest ('how many times would this have paged me') has to update live as both handles move, and near-misses that crossed the line but didn't dwell long enough need to read visibly differently from ones that actually would have fired. Pick meter-threshold-trip instead for a read-only dashboard status indicator with no authoring surface at all — it has no drag handles, `value` is its only input, and its identity is the asymmetric trip/re-arm latch (hysteresis), which sear-notch deliberately does not have: sear-notch's live state is a pure, unlatched function of current dwell, because here the duration clause itself is the thing being tuned, not a fixed pair of marks.
instruction: Renders an alert rule — threshold + required dwell duration — as a notch cut into a historical sparkline instead of two separate number inputs. Props: `data` (an ascending `{t, v}[]` series, `t` in elapsed ms), `liveValue` (current reading, defaults to the last sample), `min`/`max` (display domain, defaults padded from `data`), `unit`, `metricLabel`, `windowLabel` (the backtest window's name, used verbatim in readouts, e.g. 'past 1h'), controlled/uncontrolled `threshold`/`defaultThreshold` + `onThresholdChange`, and controlled/uncontrolled `forMs`/`defaultForMs` (default 60000) + `onForChange`. GEOMETRY: the sparkline is one SVG polyline; a notch is drawn near the series' live edge as two vertical 'shoulders' running from a top rail down to a horizontal 'floor' bar — the floor bar's height is the threshold, the gap between the shoulders is the duration, both rendered directly inside the chart, not as separate controls beside it. CLASSIFICATION (the falsifiable core): every contiguous span of `data` above `threshold` is found by walking the series once and linearly interpolating the EXACT crossing time between the two straddling samples (never snapping to a sample, never a coarser 'did the peak cross the line' test) to get that excursion's real duration; it is then classified solely by comparing that duration to `forMs` — fired = duration >= forMs — which is mathematically the same dwell-fraction test the live sear runs (d = elapsed-above / forMs, fired = d >= 1), just evaluated once at the excursion's own end instead of every frame. A fired excursion's area (curve down to the threshold line) renders as a solid `fill-current text-foreground` polygon; a near-miss that crossed but never dwelled long enough renders hollow — `fill-none`, dashed `text-ns-muted` outline — so narrowing the duration handle while watching visibly flips excursions from hollow to solid the instant their real duration reaches the new `forMs`, which is the entire point of the duration handle and could not be shown by a simpler crossing-only test. The backtest count ('would have fired N times {windowLabel}') is plain tabular-nums text recomputed synchronously on every pointermove of either handle — never debounced, since a debounce reads as a server round-trip and erodes trust in the number. INTERACTION: two real DOM elements carry the drag, not the (aria-hidden) SVG — a `role=slider aria-orientation=vertical` div whose hit area spans the chart's full plot height at the notch's x-position (dragging it maps pointer Y to threshold continuously, no snapping) and a `role=slider aria-orientation=horizontal` div covering a fixed band right of the notch's anchor (dragging it maps pointer X to a continuous half-width, log-interpolated against the four duration anchors in pixel-space so intermediate positions still produce a sensible in-between `forMs` for the live count) that snaps its width to the nearest of 30s/1m/5m/15m on release via a settle transition — the durations a real alerting backend accepts, not an arbitrary continuous value. Both are fully keyboard operable: Up/Right and Down/Left step (threshold by domain/100 per step, Home/End to the domain rails; duration by one bucket, Home/End to 30s/15m), each commit re-running the same classification. SEAR MECHANISM: beside the chart, a small pivoting SVG catch and an adjacent fill gauge visualize the metric's CURRENT live dwell, independent of the historical backtest — one scalar, d = (continuous time `liveValue` has stayed above `threshold`) / `forMs`, drives everything: the catch's rotation is `d` times its fixed engagement arc, the gauge's fill height is `d`, and firing is exactly `d >= 1` — no separate latch or boolean, zero independent choreography. The instant `liveValue` drops back to or below `threshold`, dwell resets to 0 and the catch un-cocks immediately — deliberately NOT the hysteresis this registry's meter-threshold-trip uses, because here the duration clause is itself the tunable rule, not a fixed trip/re-arm pair. A11y: the outer label ties both sliders together via `aria-labelledby`; each slider's `aria-valuetext` is the same composite sentence — 'threshold {value}{unit} for {duration} — would have fired {n} times {windowLabel}' — so either control alone answers the backtest question by voice; the fired count is also plain visible text, never aria-only; the sparkline, notch SVG and sear SVG are all `aria-hidden`, decorative once the sliders and text carry the real semantics; a visually-hidden `role=status aria-live=polite` region announces the same composite sentence plus the live status ('clear' / 'armed — N% to firing' / 'firing now'), updated only on drag release or a keyboard commit, never on every raw pointermove. Reduced motion (via `matchMedia` with a live listener): the sear's rotation stops sweeping continuously with `d` and instead snaps directly between its rest position, its engaged position (while dwelling, whatever the exact `d`) and its released position (at fired) — no interpolated sweep — while the fill gauge, being data, not decoration, keeps tracking `d` exactly. Every stroke and fill is a token utility class (`text-foreground`, `text-ns-muted`, `text-border`, `text-ns-accent` only on an actively grabbed or focused handle) — no hex, no canvas, no getComputedStyle, DOM+SVG+CSS only.
